spCVAudit

Compare spatial cross-validation with the places where you need predictions.

spCVAudit compares validation-to-training distances with target-to-training distances, adds information about spatial correlation, and helps you assess candidate CV schemes. It implements the nearest-neighbour contrasts and Gaussian reference calculations in Nearest-neighbour distances and prediction error in spatial cross-validation.

Website and tutorials · Paper and reproducibility code · Report a problem

Install 

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("olatunjijohnson/spCVAudit")

The tutorials are available on the website. To also install local copies for vignette(package = "spCVAudit"), use:

install.packages(c("knitr", "rmarkdown"))
remotes::install_github("olatunjijohnson/spCVAudit", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Version 0.1.0 is available from GitHub. It is prepared for CRAN submission but has not been submitted to, or accepted by, CRAN. Core calculations use only base and recommended R packages. Install sf for projected spatial objects and CAST for the optional kNNDM constructor.

A first comparison 

library(spCVAudit)

# Numeric coordinates must share a projected coordinate system and units.
set.seed(42)
training <- matrix(runif(160), ncol = 2)
target <- prediction_target(
  as.matrix(expand.grid(x = seq(0.05, 0.95, length.out = 10),
                       y = seq(0.05, 0.95, length.out = 10)))
)

schemes <- list(
  random = spatial_folds(training, k = 5, method = "random", seed = 1),
  block = spatial_folds(training, k = 5, method = "block", seed = 1)
)

covariance <- spatial_covariance(range = 0.2, signal = 0.8)
comparison <- compare_cv_schemes(training, schemes, target, covariance,
                                 criterion = "J2")
comparison
plot(comparison$audits$random)

This comparison chooses the smallest absolute J2. It does not use target responses or choose the smallest observed prediction error. Every tied scheme receives an explicit selection probability.

What the diagnostics tell you

Quantity Meaning
A Mean target nearest distance minus mean validation nearest distance
W Overall difference between the two nearest-distance distributions
J1 Validation minus target mean nearest-observation correlation
J2 Validation minus target mean squared nearest-observation correlation
U1, U2 Unsigned discrepancies between correlation and squared-correlation distributions

W = 0 means the nearest-distance distributions match. J2 = 0 means their mean squared correlations match. Neither guarantees unbiased CV for a model that uses all training observations.

For Gaussian prediction using one neighbour, with known mean and covariance, target MSE minus expected CV MSE equals total response variance times J2. gaussian_cv() calculates the full-neighbour MSE difference, separates the additional-neighbour contribution, and supplies its bound under positive independent observation noise. These are model-based reference calculations, not a correction for an arbitrary fitted prediction model.

Relationship to spLeakage and the paper

spCVAudit is a focused successor to the spatial CV diagnostics developed in spLeakage. It uses the paper’s names J1 and J2, supports weighted targets and explicit ties, and exposes the Gaussian decomposition and bound. Older leakage checks and experimental error-correction functions are not part of this API. The original spLeakage package remains separate.

The paper repository preserves the exact spLeakage source snapshot and fitting procedure used for its retained results. Installing spCVAudit is not a replacement for running that fixed reproduction environment. Its tutorials identify which calculations reproduce the theory and which illustrate a new analysis.

Use citation("spCVAudit") for the software citation. The associated manuscript, supplementary material, data attribution and complete reproduction instructions are in the linked paper repository. No publication DOI is claimed before one is assigned.
